title: 1998 AHSME Problem 2
statement: Letters \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) and \(D\) represent four different digits selected from \(0,\) \(1,\) \(2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(9.\) If \(\frac{A+B}{C+D}\) is an integer that is as large as possible, what is the value of \(A+B?\)

solutions.text: The least positive denominator is \(0+1=1,\) and the greatest numerator using two other digits is \(8+9=17.\) Their ratio is the integer \(17,\) which is plainly maximal. Thus \(A+B=17,\) and E is correct.
hints: Make the denominator as small as possible using distinct digits
The two smallest digits and the two largest digits are disjoint pairs
